chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Moving to Lynchburg in 1972 on Fess Williams's tip
summary: Fess Williams told him of a job in Lynchburg, Virginia; he worked there and Charlottesville through the seventies.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, it's the downstairs of the Empire State Building. So those were two stand-out jobs. But then I would have to go back to the club date thing again. So that was mainly the sixties, you know, you're doin' whatever you can do. So I decided I'd have to make a change. So I got a call. Fess Williams, who used to have a band at the Vendome in Chicago, and he played clarinet and he became an official at the union...then I met his two sons, who were saxophone players and we became friends through the years, you know, they both played tenor, Rudy and I forget his brother's name. Anyway, he says, "Nick, there's a thing down in Lynchburg you can have, I was just down there." But you know he didn't want to stay there. He says, "Why don't you call this fella and you can go on down there." I says, "Yeah, shoot, I need to go somewhere. So that's how I happened to go to Lynchburg. And I worked steady, between Lynchburg and Charlottesville, for practically all the seventies. Yeah.
You went there first in what year?

'72. Yeah. And this was, you know, a small community, but they had a nice club. The guy that owned the place was from Detroit and he was a big city man and he went down in there and he liked music. I had a good relationship; I made some nice friends there. Then after we left Lynchburg, then we came to Charlottesville, you know, and worked. And we worked steady, you know, right on up...
The same group? You brought a group with you?

No, no. It was a group that was there. It was Tommy Miller. It was an organ player and singer, very talented, he sings like Ray Charles, Nat King Cole, Billy Eckstine and he played organ, you know. And we had drums and myself, you know. We were entertainment because of my show business which I had learned and with his entertainment we were able to work, you know what I mean. We made money for everybody we worked for, you know.
